errors.text_span: The graph displays the trends of four different economic indicators over time
errors.evidence: The chart displays five distinct lines, as detailed in the legend, not four. There are two lines for HVPI and two for Bruttostundenlöhne und -gehälter, based on different index periods.
The x-axis in the figure extends to July 2025, not January 2025.

errors.text_span: with labels at every other year.
errors.evidence: The x-axis has labels for January and July of every year, meaning there are two labels per year, not one every other year.
The maroon line (Mindestlohn) has a value of approximately 116 in January 2022, not 114.

errors.text_span: The HVPI is depicted as a light green line, beginning at 100 in January 2015, increasing gradually to around 105 in mid-2017, and then rising to around 115 in January 2022, with a further increase to around 125 in January 2023, and reaching around 130 in January 2025.
errors.evidence: This description incorrectly merges two separate lines (light green and dark green) into one continuous trend. The light green line ends in mid-2022 around 118. The dark green line starts in late 2022 at ~141 and ends at 150. The values reported for 2023 (~125) and 2025 (~130) are incorrect for either line and appear to be hallucinated.

errors.text_span: with a notable jump to around 140 in January 2023, and continuing to rise to around 155 in January 2025.
errors.evidence: This description incorrectly merges the light blue and dark blue lines. The light blue line ends in mid-2022. The dark blue line is a separate series that starts in late 2022 at a value of ~141. Describing this as a 'jump' in a single line is a misrepresentation of the chart's structure.

errors.text_span: The adjusted HVPI and Bruttostundenlöhne und -gehälter, represented by dark green and dark blue lines respectively, remain relatively stable around 100 until January 2023
errors.evidence: This is entirely false. The dark green and dark blue lines do not exist before late 2022. They start at a value of approximately 141.2, not 100. The description invents a history for these lines that is not present in the chart.
